diagnostic_evidence.quote: not able to do so for a few criteria, including

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract says every listed criterion (including Frobenius-norm minimization, Schatten p-norm minimization and condition minimization, p>2, and stable-rank maximization) is NP hard and has no PTAS. The paper shows Frobenius-norm minimization is polynomial. It also proves no PTAS for only some criteria: the Table and Introduction concede that no gap was obtained for Schatten p-norm minimization, the p-norm condition numbers, the mixed p-condition number and the p-stable rank.

failure_location.quote: are NP hard and do not admit polynomial time approximation schemes (PTAS).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the abstract to list exactly the criteria for which NP-hardness and no-PTAS are proved, and exclude Frobenius-norm minimization.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised scope of the paper is overstated. The no-PTAS conclusion is not established for several criteria named in the abstract.
issues.title: Abstract claims NP-hardness and no PTAS for all listed criteria, contradicting the body
issues.why_classification: Only the scope statement needs rewording; no theorem or proof changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper states interlacing for A of arbitrary size, with no assumption on m and n. For m<n the lower bound is wrong: A=[e1 e2 e1] in R^{2x3} and C=[e1 e2] give sigma_1(A)=sqrt2 > sigma_1(C)=1, contradicting sigma_{min{m,n}-k+j}(A) <= sigma_j(C) at j=1. The correct index for deleting n-k columns is n-k+j, with zero padding.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict (e_inter) to m>=n, or replace min{m,n} by n and pad with zeros.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed inequality is false as stated. Later uses apply it only to tall full-column-rank C, where it is correct, so no result is invalidated.
issues.title: Singular value interlacing (e_inter) is false for wide matrices
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the statement suffices and every later use survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where inputs are rational numbers and the input size is measured in the number of bits.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper adopts the Turing model with rational inputs measured in bits. The decision problems require unit-norm columns, and the reduction produces entries 1/sqrt3, which are irrational. Thresholds such as 2sqrt2/3 and sqrt(3/2) are irrational too. The output is therefore not a legitimate instance of the stated decision problems, so 'polynomial-time reduction' is not established in the declared model.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either switch to a real-number computation model, or rescale to 0/1 columns and restate the decision problems and the optimal-value lemmas for non-normalized columns with rational (e.g. squared) thresholds.
issues.overall_effect: Every NP-hardness and gap result uses this construction, so all of them are formally unsupported in the stated bit model.
issues.title: X3C reduction outputs irrational matrices although inputs are declared rational
issues.why_classification: The hardness idea survives, but the problem formulations and the normalization-based lemmas must be restated, which is a contained but nontrivial change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The decision problems: volume maximization and S-optimality maximization are NP hard.

issues.failure_explanation: NP completeness requires membership in NP, which is never addressed. Verifying vol(C)>=b or sopt(C)>=b means comparing determinants or singular values of real matrices, and the paper's own reduction uses irrational entries. Theorem t_voldec and the Table assert only NP hardness.

failure_location.quote: and S-optimality maximization are NP complete (Section~\ref{s_volume1}),

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'NP complete' by 'NP hard', or add a proof of membership in NP.
issues.overall_effect: The section overstates what is established; the formal result is only NP hardness.
issues.title: Section 3 claims NP completeness; only NP hardness is proved
issues.why_classification: A one-word change to the claim suffices.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\sqrt{1+\tfrac{1}{4k}}$. Thus, unless P=NP, there is no PTAS for Frobenius norm minimization of the pseudo-inverse.

issues.failure_explanation: In the reduction k=M grows with the instance. The proved gaps are (2sqrt2/3)^{1/k} for S-optimality, and sqrt(1+1/(4k)) for the Frobenius and Schatten-p pseudo-inverse norms and the Frobenius condition number. These tend to 1 as k grows. For a fixed epsilon, a (1-epsilon)- or (1+epsilon)-approximation does not separate yes from no instances once k is large, so no contradiction with P!=NP follows. The 'no PTAS' conclusion needs a gap bounded away from 1 independent of k.

failure_location.quote: $(2\sqrt{2}/3)^{1/k}$. Thus, unless P=NP, there is no PTAS for S-optimality maximization.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a constant gap independent of k must be proved (the argument only adds 1/4 to the squared Frobenius norm). Otherwise retract the no-PTAS claims for these four criteria and state only k-dependent hardness.
issues.overall_effect: The no-PTAS claims for S-optimality, Frobenius and Schatten-p pseudo-inverse minimization, and Frobenius condition number minimization are unsupported. Only NP-hardness of the decision problems remains.
issues.title: Gaps that shrink to 1 as k grows do not rule out a PTAS
issues.why_classification: The claim cannot be kept without a new gap construction, and the fallback of retracting it loses four advertised no-PTAS results.

issues.failure_explanation: The decision problems quantify over all k-column submatrices C of A, while Lemma l_pinv and the no-PTAS inductions assume rank(C)=k. For rank-deficient C the bounds fail: C=[e1 e1] has ||C^dagger||_2=1/sqrt2<1. X3C-derived A can have rank-deficient M-column submatrices, for example {1,2,3}+{4,5,6}={1,2,4}+{3,5,6} as incidence vectors. Such C could make a 'no' instance look like 'yes' at b=1, and could violate the sqrt(3/2) and k+1/4 lower bounds.

failure_location.quote: The proof for all the norms is the same as that of Theorem~\ref{t_voldec} but uses Lemma~\ref{l_pinv} instead.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the pseudo-inverse problems to full-column-rank submatrices (or set the norm to +infinity when rank<k). Yes-instances give orthonormal, hence full-rank, C, so the arguments then go through.
issues.overall_effect: The equivalence 'yes iff orthonormal' and the gap lower bounds are unproved for pseudo-inverse criteria unless rank deficiency is excluded.
issues.title: Pseudo-inverse hardness and gaps ignore rank-deficient column subsets
issues.why_classification: A short change to the problem definition fixes the gap, and the proofs, thresholds and conclusions remain.

issues.failure_explanation: rvol(C)=1 only forces all singular values to be equal, not equal to 1, since rvol is scale invariant. For example C=2I has rvol=1 but its columns are not orthonormal. The lemma is stated for arbitrary full-column-rank C with no normalization, so its 'if and only if' is false, and the proof's step to 'equal to 1' is unjustified.

failure_location.quote: Hence, all singular values of $\mc$ are equal to~1, and $\mc$ has orthonormal columns.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis ||Ce_j||_2=1, or state that equality holds iff C is a positive multiple of a matrix with orthonormal columns.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma is false as stated. Theorem thm:rvolnp applies it to unit-norm columns, where it holds, so its use is unaffected.
issues.title: Relative-volume lemma: equality does not force orthonormal columns
issues.why_classification: Adding the unit-norm hypothesis, already present wherever the lemma is used, repairs it.

issues.failure_explanation: From sigma_1>=1 one gets k/sigma_1^p <= k, so (k/sigma_1^p)^{1/p} <= k^{1/p}. The displayed chain claims the reverse, '>= k^{1/p}', so the lower bound ||C^dagger||_{(p)} >= k^{1/p} is not proved. The claim is true by Jensen/power-mean applied to sum sigma_j^{-p} under sum sigma_j^2=k, or by the function g used later in the equality part, but the stated proof is invalid. The Frobenius case is declared a special case of this part.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the inequality via Jensen/power-mean on sigma_j^2 with sum sigma_j^2=k, or by summing g(sigma_j)>=0 from the equality argument.
issues.overall_effect: The lower-bound half of Lemma l_pinv for p>=2 is unproved as written. Theorem t_pi7 needs it so that the value k^{1/p} is attained only by orthonormal C.
issues.title: Schatten-p pseudo-inverse lower bound uses an inequality in the wrong direction
issues.why_classification: The statement is true and a short standard inequality replaces the faulty step.

issues.failure_explanation: For q=p/2>1, the Schatten q-norm of a block-diagonal matrix is (a^q+b^q)^{1/q}, not a+b, and (a^q+b^q)^{1/q} < a+b. The step 'norm of diag = sum of norms' is therefore wrong, and the squared-norm lemma is false for p>2. Counterexample: C=I_2, C1=e1, C2=e2, p=4 gives ||C^dagger||_(4)^2 = sqrt2 < 2 = ||C1^dagger||_(4)^2+||C2^dagger||_(4)^2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State and prove the p-th power version ||C^dagger||_(p)^p >= ||C1^dagger||_(p)^p + ||C2^dagger||_(p)^p, using the correct block-diagonal norm in the pinching step.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised 'p-norm bounds for partitioned pseudo-inverses' (contribution 6) is false as stated. No later proof uses it.
issues.title: Partitioned Schatten-p pseudo-inverse bound is false and its proof treats a block-diagonal norm as a sum
issues.why_classification: The same proof architecture works for a weaker, recognizably comparable inequality, but the stated result must change and the squared version is lost.
